Refined and Creative Vietnamese Cuisine
Aug 2026 • Solo
Thịt Đông Jelly Beef - I loved the variety of flavors in this dish and how every component had a role to play. There was also an interesting play on textures that made each bite more enjoyable. The beef flavor was persistent; even five minutes later, I could still taste it lingering on my tongue. The nước chấm also elevated the dish, providing just enough acidity to brighten the other flavors. 

Foie Gras Spring Roll - The filling was really soft and tender, although I wish the exterior had been crispier, especially since this was a spring roll. It wasn't very greasy. I liked the acidity that the mango brûlée brought to the dish. What impressed me most was that no single flavor dominated the bite. I could distinctly taste the foie gras, pork, herbs, and mango brûlée while still enjoying them together. This dish was well executed, and I would gladly ask for more rolls.

Le Petit Bánh Mì - This was a creative take on bánh mì, but I would still say a traditional bánh mì is better. The air baguette was almost entirely filled with pâté, so I thought the filling-to-bread ratio was excessive. It felt like 95% filling, with the bread mostly serving as a thin outer layer. I wanted more of that bread texture to balance the richness of the filling. Nonetheless, the dish itself was rich and flavorful.

Bánh Ram Ít Dumpling - This was really good and extremely savory, with a nice combination of softness and crunch. I could clearly taste the sticky rice, and despite all the seafood components, the dish wasn't overly salty. It wasn't greasy at all either. 

Crab & Asparagus - I could detect hints of both the crab and sea urchin, but I don't think their flavors came through strongly enough because the curry overpowered the seafood. As a result, the dish didn't feel as complex as I expected from its ingredients. The white asparagus, however, was fresh and slightly sweet, which complemented the natural sweetness of the crab.

Salmon Waffle Tart - I loved how aesthetically pleasing this dish was. I also liked that everything remained intact with every bite, especially since it took me at least three bites to finish it. The dill cream wasn't heavy; it was smooth and creamy, with enough tanginess to balance the saltiness of the smoked salmon and roe. The Vietnamese-French fusion was definitely evident here, particularly through the combination of bánh nhúng with the more classic French-inspired toppings.

Scallop & Sweet Corn - The sweetness in this dish was elegant and very well controlled. The scallop already provided its own natural sweetness, while the sauce wasn't overly sweet, keeping the overall sweetness at just the right level. Despite having several naturally sweet ingredients, the dish never became one-dimensional. 

Blue River Prawn - The prawn was juicy, succulent, and properly cooked. However, I was hoping for more of a smoky aroma or charred flavor from the grilling. The sauce was rich without being very salty and complemented the prawn. I also wish the young coconut noodles had been given more justice, as there were only around two or three strands on the plate, which wasn't really enough for me to appreciate the component properly. The pomelo was fresh and provided enough acidity to balance the richness of the dish.

Five Spice & Orange Duck - The duck was tender and juicy, with a strong and distinctive flavor. I also enjoyed the duck sausage, which was savory and had a nice charred quality. The sauce was peppery without being harsh, and there was enough of it to accompany the meat throughout the dish. Overall, I thought the sweet and savory elements were balanced.

Caviar Box - This was a surprising dish for me because I had never tried caviar with fruit and white chocolate before. Unfortunately, I wouldn't say the combination completely worked. The dish leaned heavily toward sweetness, while I was looking for more salinity from the caviar. I'm not sure whether the relatively mild salinity was characteristic of the particular Đà Lạt caviar used, but either way, the sweetness didn't complement the caviar well for me. It actually made me question whether the caviar needed to be there at all or whether its inclusion was more about adding a luxurious ingredient than improving the dish.

Since this is a Michelin-starred restaurant, I went into the meal with higher expectations and had a higher standard for each dish. That's why I was surprised to come away with only one favorite, which was the Bánh Ram Ít Dumpling, out of the ten dishes served. There were several dishes I enjoyed, and I still had a great experience dining here, but I was expecting more, given that this is Vietnam's first Michelin-starred restaurant.

The service, however, was great. The staff contributed positively to the experience. My main issue with the dining room itself was the spacing. The tables were positioned quite close together, and with other diners immediately to my left and right, I felt a little claustrophobic.

A few too many "buts"....
Aug 2026 • Family
We ordered from the a la carte menu and not one of those proposed. 
The premise is that the food isn't bad, but:
- some portions are truly of modest quantity
- the location is on a street where there is a permanent local market that isn't exactly elegant (personally, I didn't mind it, aside from a rat crossing the street, but it's still an aspect not to be underestimated, also in terms of prices)
- the dining rooms and the spacing are not appropriate for a restaurant of this type
- the table setting is practically absent
- the timing of the courses was not respected, dishes served without coordination for the table
- vegetarian dishes (except perhaps one) = "normal" menu dish - meat / fish (the balance?)
- staff willing and nice but not really professional
I won't go into the technical aspect of the cooking because I find that eating at least well is the minimum requirement, but you also go to a restaurant of this type for the overall experience and this, alas, was disappointing. 
Given what I've said, I must say that the price-to-quality ratio is definitely unbalanced considering we are in Vietnam, therefore with certain types of costs for staff, rent, raw materials, etc. I reiterate that I didn't eat anything bad; a little more organization, a few dollars less, and a little more attention to some aspects that I understand require energy and effort would suffice, and I think we would start to get there...

Incredible food, but rushed like an assembly line
Jun 2026 • Couples
My experience here was a heartbreaking contradiction. On one hand, the kitchen is executing at an elite level; on the other, the front-of-house team is running the dining room like a high-speed assembly line.
Let’s start with the positives: the food was absolutely phenomenal. Every single dish across the 10-course degustation menu was beautifully conceptualized, technically flawless, and bursting with flavor. The kitchen team clearly possesses immense talent and deserves recognition for what they put on the plate.
Unfortunately, the service entirely derailed the evening. Despite paying a premium price for a high-end dining experience, we were treated less like individual guests and more like cattle being herded through a system. Because the restaurant serves the degustation concurrently, we were forced into the exact same rhythm as everyone else in the room. There was zero personalization or attentiveness to our pace. Waitstaff were constantly hovering, aggressively trying to clear our plates before we had even finished our last bites. It felt less like a relaxed, luxurious dinner and more like a race against a stopwatch.
To make matters worse, the matching wine pairing was a complete letdown. The pours were incredibly small—bordering on stingy—and offered absolutely no value for the steep price tag attached to them.
To top off a frustrating night, a hefty mandatory service charge was tacked onto the bill. Forced tipping is hard to swallow at the best of times, but when a meal is already expensive and the service is this rushed and impersonal, it feels like an insult.
If you only care about what is on the plate, the food won't disappoint. But if you expect a premium price tag to come with premium hospitality, respect for your time, and a relaxed atmosphere, you will likely leave feeling as ripped off as we did.

Fantastic Return
Jun 2026 • Solo
Returning to ANAN Saigon - @anansaigon - after a year, I was struck by how the restaurant continues to master the delicate art of evolution without alienation. Nestled within the gritty, pulsating heart of the Chợ Cũ market, the iconic “tube house” setting remains a masterclass in atmospheric contrast—a polished, vibrant sanctuary that feels entirely at home amidst the city’s chaotic energy.

@petercuongfranklin Chef Peter Cuong Franklin’s “Cuisine Mới” philosophy is on full display here. What remains most impressive is the unwavering consistency in his vision: an ability to deconstruct and elevate the soul of Vietnamese street culture through a sophisticated, refined lens. Every course is a testament to his deep respect for local roots, where the heritage of the flavors is never lost, even as they are reimagined through modern technique.

The service is warm, knowledgeable, and distinctly convivial, mirroring the unpretentious spirit of Saigon itself. It is a rare, high-octane dining experience that manages to be both intellectually stimulating and deeply comforting. 

ANAN remains a vital pulse in Vietnam’s gastronomic scene, proving that true culinary innovation is about honoring the past with every forward-thinking bite. A triumphant return.

Well worth the first Michelín star!
Jun 2026 • Couples
We dined last weekend at Anan Saigon, and it completely blew us away. Nestled right in the vibrant heart of the Ton That Dam Street market, Chef Peter Cuong Franklin’s one-Michelin-star gem is a brilliant beacon of "Cuisine Mới" (modern Vietnamese cuisine).

We treated ourselves to the "Culinary Journey Through Vietnam" tasting menu, and every single dish was a masterpiece. We loved how the chef paired elegance and textures in the "Foie Gras Spring Roll," while the whimsical "Le Petit Bánh Mì" was pure genius. The absolute highlight for us was the "Caviar Box Đà Lạt"—we’ve never had caviar served as a dessert before, yet this was in the pure tradition of sweet / salted Vietnamese savours. "Strangely delicious" 😋 

Beautifully focused lighting that made our plates look stunning. Combined with flawless service and multiple table visits from the friendly chef, Anan is easily one of our favorite restaurants in Asia!

5-stars!
Apr 2026 • Couples
Anan Saigon is certainly expensive by local standards, but when you consider it’s a full tasting menu at a 1-Michelin star restaurant for roughly $100 USD per person, it feels like a fantastic value. We made a reservation for two several weeks in advance via email and the process was incredibly easy.

The restaurant is tucked into the middle of the market area just off central District 1, within walking distance of the Reverie Saigon where we were staying. Anan occupies a narrow traditional Saigon-style home converted into a multi-level dining space, with the restaurant on the lower floors and their related cocktail bar, Nhau Nhau, upstairs. The whole place has a stylish, energetic vibe while still feeling intimate and distinctly local.

Service was polished to Western fine dining standards, which makes sense given that many of the diners appeared to be international visitors. Every member of the staff spoke fluent English and explained each dish thoughtfully and clearly.

We chose the Saigon tasting menu, which began with amuse-bouche bites before progressing through seven courses plus dessert. The standout for me was the “Le Petit Banh Mi” — a playful bite-sized interpretation of Vietnam’s iconic sandwich, filled with pâté and beef while still delivering the crispiness you expect from a proper baguette. Creative, delicious, and memorable. I also loved the Ha Noi turmeric fish. The cod was cooked perfectly, with the sweetness of the fish balancing beautifully against the earthy turmeric and flavorful sauce.

Dessert was outstanding. As someone who loves Vietnamese coffee, I thought the combination of robusta coffee bitterness, chocolate, and coconut jelly was incredibly well executed. The textures and flavors all complemented each other beautifully.

The cocktail menu also looked very inventive, and I imagine that creativity extends upstairs to Nhau Nhau bar. Unfortunately we didn’t have time to visit, but I definitely would on a future trip.

While Anan is undeniably a splurge for Vietnam, the creativity, execution, service, and overall experience make it absolutely worth it for travelers looking for a memorable dining experience in Saigon. There are not many places in the world where you can enjoy a Michelin-starred tasting menu of this caliber for around $100 USD per person.

Superb food, average atmosphere and service for the $$$
Mar 2026 • Couples
We were keen to visit one of the many Micheline star restaurants across Vietnam as part of our trip and Anan Saigon came highly recommended. We pre-booked the Chef's tasting menu with wine pairing - $230 per person.

The restaurant is location in one of Ho Chi Minh's wet markets so an interesting walk to find it. The restaurant itself is located across the florrs of an old residential style building so lots of very small rooms. We were early so started with a coktail at Nhau Nhau on the roof - which also serves some of the tasting menu disches as a la carte options. Cocktail options were limited but interesting, however my husbands drink was served in a plastic glass which is a little naff for a michelin restaurant.

We were then taken downstairs t the restaurant - a small, very modern room with maybe 10-12 tables - a little cramped and close together and lacking the atmosphere I expected. The staff explained the concept of the tasting menu and went to collect our first course. When the first course was served we had to remind the staff that we also wanted the wine pairing even though it was clearly noted on our reservation. 

The food is incredibly prepared - stunning to look at, great interpretations of classic vietnamese dishes and in most cases not what we would order in a restaurant so a great chance to try different dishes. The pase the dishes are served is good and the staff are very passionate about the dishes and describing the region that influences them, the chefs preperation style and how best to enjoy them.

In summary - it was a good experience but not great and for the extortionate price being charged it should be great. The atmosphere in the restaurant is sterile - it feels like a dentist waiting room, not a restaurant. The staff are good but not great - we were never asked if wanted other drinks, our package should have included a desert cocktail which never arrived and we were interrogated if we didnt finish a dish! There is a lot of choice across Vietnam if you want to visit a Michelin star restauant and I'm not sure this is the best there is to try?
